question.problem: Which of the following sets of parametric equations, defined for $t\in (-\infty ,\infty ),$ generate a vertical parabola that has its vertex at $(-2,3)$ and which passes through the point $(-10,-5)?$
question.worked_solution:
The parametric equations of a vertical parabola that has its vertex at $(h,k)$ are

$$
x-h=2pt,\,y-k=p{t}^{2},
$$

where $p$ is constant.

In our case, $(h,k)=(-2,3),$ and so we have

$$
x+2=2pt,\,y-3=p{t}^{2}.
$$

Since the parabola passes through $(-10,-5),$ we can substitute $x=-10$ and $y=-5$ into the parametric equations to obtain a system of equations. This gives

$$
\{\begin{aligned}-8=2pt \\ -8=p{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Solving the first equation for $t,$ we have

$$
\begin{aligned}-8 & =2pt \\ t & =-\frac{4}{p}.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting this into the second equation and solving for $p,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}-8 & =p{(-\frac{4}{p})}^{2} \\ -8 & =p\cdot \frac{16}{{p}^{2}} \\ -1 & =\frac{2}{p} \\ p & =-2.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the parametric equations of the parabola are

$$
x+2=2(-2)t,\,y-3=(-2){t}^{2},
$$

which simplify to

$$
x+2=-4t,\,y-3=-2{t}^{2}.
$$
